findings       3, worst first
  MEDIUM    no-node-health  1 accelerator node has no node health detection: bad nodes keep getting work
            confidence likely
            evidence  no node-problem-detector, no EKS node monitoring agent, and every node condition is one of the kubelet's five
            fix       First option: keep GKE node auto-repair on for the accelerator pools (it repairs nodes whose GPU device or driver fails). Otherwise install node-problem-detector as the stack's node_health, with a kernel-log rule that sets GPUProblem on a fatal NVIDIA Xid.
                      the KCL change is in --json (findings[].fix.kcl_diff)
            docs      https://github.com/kubernetes/node-problem-detector
  MEDIUM    shm-too-small  1 workload runs accelerators with the 64 MiB /dev/shm default
            evidence  Job/research/train: 1 pod, container trainer mounts no memory emptyDir at /dev/shm
            fix       Mount an emptyDir {medium: Memory} (with a sizeLimit) at /dev/shm in each accelerator container: NCCL, PyTorch DataLoader workers and vLLM's tensor parallelism need more than 64 MiB.
  INFO      image-volumes-unavailable  Image volumes are unavailable: weights cannot be mounted from an OCI artifact without a sidecar
            evidence  API server v1.31.2-gke.1000: the ImageVolume feature gate is on by default from Kubernetes 1.35
                      Node/gke-gpu-h100-0: containerd 1.7.24, image volumes need 2.1+
            fix       Upgrade to Kubernetes 1.35+ with containerd 2.1+ to mount weights as an image volume. Until then, KServe's modelcar sidecar or an init-container copy is the fallback.
            docs      https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#image

proposal       the ml.k below is printed only: place it with --env <env> (deploy/kcl/<env>/ml.k) or --out <file>, then --write
               wire it into deploy/kcl/<env>/main.k:
                   import .ml
                   ml_stacks = ml.ml_stacks   # in its forge.Bundle
